name: com.lyra-ui/mcp
title: Lyra UI
description: Search Lyra UI web components in 81 languages and read exact component APIs and docs.

tools.name: search_components
tools.description:
Ranked search over the Lyra UI component catalog.

Call this before concluding a component is missing — most apparent gaps are naming
mismatches. No authentication, no side effects.

locale.title: Locale
locale.description: Locale used for returned names/descriptions (any of the site's 81 language tags, e.g. hi, zh-TW, pt-BR; legacy pt = pt-PT); all locales remain searchable.

tools.name: get_component
tools.description:
Return one component's complete generated Markdown API reference.

Prefer this exact lookup after `search_components` identifies a tag. It includes properties,
attributes, events, slots, CSS parts, themeable custom properties, usage, and known gotchas.

tools.name: search_documentation
tools.description: Search section-sized chunks of the component and library-wide Markdown reference.

tag.title: Tag
tag.description: Optional exact component tag to search within.

topic.title: Topic
topic.description: Optional library-guide topic to search within.

tools.name: resolve_migration
tools.description: Resolve a documented `wa-*` or `sl-*` component name to its Lyra counterpart.

tools.name: submit_request
tools.description:
Report a component you needed but could not find, and get back the closest existing ones.

Search first: most apparent gaps are naming mismatches, and `search_components` answers that
in one call without filing anything. The response here also lists close matches — read them.

If you are an agent acting for someone: ask them and get their explicit agreement before
submitting. This sends their words to a third-party service. Never file as a silent side
effect of noticing a gap.

`name` and `email` are optional; anonymous is the default. Ask the user whether they want to
be reachable — never invent an address or reuse one from git config or earlier context.

Always classify it: set `kind` to its category and `labels` to every matching sub-category
label from the schema's enum (for example `bug:keyboard` and `bug:focus`, or `scope:` when it
is not about one component family). Both fields are optional only so that older clients keep
working: a request without them waits in the maintainer's unclassified queue for manual
triage. Component and family tags are detected automatically from the `lr-*` names in your
text.

Fill in every other optional field you can as well: `use_case`, `searched_for`,
`settled_for`, `agent`, and `model` (the id of the model writing the report). Triage and the
maintainer's statistics rely on them. `name` and `email` stay opt-in, as described above.

Submissions are stored privately, shown only to the maintainer, and never published. Describe
the component generically: no source code, no client or product names, no credentials.

title.title: Title
title.description: Short, specific summary naming the missing component, bug, or API gap.

description.title: Description
description.description: Generic behavior needed or documented contract versus observed behavior. Do not include source code, client names, product names, or credentials.

use_case.title: Use Case
use_case.description: Expected: the generic context explaining why the capability is needed.

searched_for.title: Searched For
searched_for.description: Expected: terms tried before giving up. The most useful field: it records the name the caller expected.

settled_for.title: Settled For
settled_for.description: Expected when you used a workaround: what you built or used instead.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: Set this on every request: its category — bug (existing behaviour is wrong), optimization (runtime cost), size (bytes shipped), dedup (duplicated implementation), harmonization (siblings differ), improvement (engineering quality), feature (a genuinely new capability).

labels.title: Labels
labels.description: Set these on every request: every sub-category label that applies, e.g. bug:keyboard and bug:focus (a facet from another kind is fine), or scope:<value> when the request is not about one component family. Component and family tags are detected automatically from lr-* names.

agent.title: Agent
agent.description: Expected: the submitting agent or client name (e.g. claude-code).

model.title: Model
model.description: Expected on agent reports: the id of the model that wrote the submission (e.g. claude-opus-5-5).

source_url.title: Source Url
source_url.description: Optional public URL with non-sensitive context.

name.title: Name
name.description: Optional contact name, only when the user explicitly asks to be reachable.

email.title: Email
email.description: Optional. Only if you want a reply — stored privately, shown to the maintainer only, never published.

tools.name: get_request_status
tools.description:
Look up a submitted request's triage state by its id.

Returns only the status, the maintainer's note and any linked issue — never the submitted
body, and never the submitter's name or email.
